questions.question: When you pull over to the side of the road:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When driving downhill, you should brake until your speed is:
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, press the brake pedal until your vehicle reaches 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: When checking your tires, what should you avoid?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning light?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly.
Remove wheel chocks and release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly.
questions.explanation: After the system charges, test the warning light by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the braking system. The warning light should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: If you're unsure how to put out a vehicle fire, you should:
questions.explanation: If you don't know which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them handle it.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking if possible until your vehicle has slowed down.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise landing gear completely before driving. If landing gear is not fully raised, it could hit railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Only needed for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how long the trip is.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you may be able to:
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder is the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: When parking, you should:

options.text: Park in a lot with automobiles.
Park so you can pull forward when leaving.
Ask drivers of smaller vehicles to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park so you can pull forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous and should be avoided when possible. Choose a parking spot that lets you pull forward when you leave. Avoid parking near smaller vehicles to prevent maneuvering problems.

questions.question: If you drive through flowing water or a large puddle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or flowing water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down and shift into a low gear. Gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of your brake system.

questions.question: What happens as a vehicle gets heavier?

options.text: The brakes have to work harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes have to work harder.
questions.explanation: A heavier vehicle requires the brakes to work harder to stop completely.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that the air lines are not:
questions.explanation: When inspecting the convertor dolly, check that all parts work properly. The air lines must be securely attached to the glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow easy turning.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop your vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before your trip.
Travel with another driver who can share driving duties.

questions.correctAnswerText: Travel with another driver who can share driving duties.
questions.explanation: Sharing driving with another person reduces fatigue for both drivers. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system:

options.text: This is normal and not a concern.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air to prevent system pressure from getting too high. If the valve releases air, there is a problem. Have a mechanic repair it.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Helps you stay awake on long trips.
Can damage the engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage the engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Rough acceleration damages your vehicle. Always accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When turning to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Do not brake because it can cause the wheels to lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it can cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while making a quick turn to avoid a hazard. Braking could lock your wheels and cause you to skid out of control.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to shift gears. It takes practice to master this technique.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm other drivers or their vehicles
Operating a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm other drivers or their vehicles
questions.explanation: Road rage means operating a vehicle with the intent to harm other drivers or physically attack them or their vehicle. This is different from aggressive driving, which is driving in a selfish or reckless manner.
